title: The Hero Twins Receive a Call from Xibalba
subtitle: A ballgame leads to the underworld

call.author: Lewis Spence
call.translator: not applicable; Spence authored this English summary
call.locator: Spence summary · Second Book; Spence summary · Second Book, normalized characters 5743-6844
call.excerpt: It was not long, however, until Hun-Came and Vukub-Came, the princes of Xibalba, heard them at play, and decided to lure them to the Underworld as they had lured their fathers. Messengers were despatched to the house of Xmucane, who, filled with alarm, despatched a louse to carry the message to her grandsons. The louse, wishing to ensure greater speed to reach the brothers, consented to be swallowed by a toad, the toad by a serpent, and the serpent by the great bird Voc. The other animals duly liberated one another; but despite his utmost efforts, the toad could not get rid of the louse, who had played him a trick by lodging in his gums, and had not been swallowed at all. The message, however, was duly delivered, and the players returned home to take leave of their grandmother and mother. Before their departure they each planted a cane in the middle of the house, which was to acquaint those they left behind with their welfare, since it would wither if any fatal circumstance befel them. Pursuing the route their fathers had followed, they passed the river of blood and the river Papuhya.
call.note: Verbatim prose from Spence's 1908 English summary, which he says draws on Brasseur de Bourbourg's French and Ximénez's Spanish translations. This is not a direct translation of the K'iche' text.

narrativeBlocks.title: The twins play ball
narrativeBlocks.body: In Spence's summary, the twins play in their fathers' ballcourt. The rulers of Xibalba hear them and send owls as messengers to summon them.

narrativeBlocks.title: The summons is carried by owls

narrativeBlocks.title: A message travels by animal helpers
narrativeBlocks.body: The grandmother sends a louse with the message; a toad, serpent, and bird help carry it. The twins return home before leaving for Xibalba.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep the K'iche' frame specific
narrativeBlocks.body: The story belongs to the Popol Vuh material about the K'iche' Hero Twins as Spence summarizes it. It is not a generic Maya account or proof of one universal ballgame ritual.

narrativeBlocks.title: The ballgame has narrative stakes
narrativeBlocks.body: The twins' game prompts the summons, connecting play, family memory, and a journey to Xibalba.
